messages.subject: Multilevel regression model comparison: Anova doesn't work?
parts:
Hi there,

I try to do a multilevel hierachical regression analysis (HRA) and am encountering some problems with the lavaan anova, getting two warnings:

Warning messages:
1: In lavTestLRT(object = object, ..., model.names = NAMES) :
  lavaan WARNING: some models are based on a different set of observed variables
2: In lavTestLRT(object = object, ..., model.names = NAMES) :
  lavaan WARNING: some models have the same degrees of freedom

I did single level HRA before using the lm command and there I never had this problem, I could just compare to nested models with anova to check for a significant Delta R2.

My code doing it multilevel with lavaan looks something like this:

# Test model 1
lavmodeldef1 <- '
              level: 1
                WPO.res ~ SD.math

              level: 2
                WPO.res ~ SD.math
'

# Test model 2
lavmodeldef2 <- '
              level: 1
                WPO.res ~ SD.math + SR3.theta

              level: 2
                WPO.res ~ SD.math
'

lavmodel1 <- sem(model = lavmodeldef1, data = dta, cluster = "Lehrperson",estimator="mlr")
summary(lavmodel1,rsquare = TRUE)
lavmodel2 <- sem(model = lavmodeldef2, data = dta, cluster = "Lehrperson",estimator="mlr")
summary(lavmodel2,rsquare = TRUE)

anova(lavmodel1,lavmodel2)

messages.author: f6d12b388faad456
messages.subject: Re: Multilevel regression model comparison: Anova doesn't work?
parts:
Yes, Anova compares the difference in chi-square and degrees of freedom, so it cannot compare two models with zero degrees of freedom (neither two models with different variables).

what I understand in your code, you might be able to compare the models changing the model 1 syntax to:

lavmodeldef1 <- ' level: 1 WPO.res ~ SD.math + 0 * SR3.theta level: 2 WPO.res ~ SD.math + 0 * SR3.theta

This way, both models have the exact same variables and different degrees of freedom.

Best regards,

Yago
